findings: F1 (supersedes the band premise): the frozen core's constraint-SELECTION order is request-level NONDETERMINISTIC whenever >=2 constraints are violated, at BOTH granularity levels (across fields AND within a field). The 096 run-001 L09/L10 'first-field law' samples (subtopicCode-first / vote-first) were single draws from that distribution - NOT a reproducible port defect. NO schema field reordering is lawful; the T-MIG-080 F3 declaration-order reading and the live wire are reconciled by nondeterminism, not by a contradicting law.

F2 (the real deterministic divergences): rating/vote carry @NotBlank ONLY on the frozen DTOs - blank (8/8) and whitespace-only (6/6) values serve 'rating: must not be blank' / 'vote: must not be blank' deterministically. The port's bare z.string().min(1) served 'must be greater than or equal to 1' - a message the core NEVER serves for these fields (outside the captured distribution), and whitespace-only values passed validation entirely (reaching the service as a vocabulary bad_request where core 400s notBlank).

F3 (parity classes of record): single-constraint payloads are byte-pinnable and the port agrees 1:1 on every pre-existing class (absent->notblank, size-only->size, pattern-only->pattern, all 6 legs per surface). Multi-constraint payloads: golden parity = status 400 + error validation_failed + message MEMBERSHIP in the violated-constraint distribution; the port serves its declared-order member deterministically, which is within the core distribution on every leg after the F2 fix.
F4 (zero-write): every matrix/battery leg carries >=1 violated constraint -> all answers 400 validation_failed on both planes across 100+ requests; zero prod writes.
